title: OneMind app manifest (onemind.app/v1, and v1alpha1 until the freeze completes)
description: apps/<id>/onemind.app.yaml, as fixed by sdk/contracts/poc-v0.md section 4, extended by section 9.3 (metadata.links, metadata.upstream, metadata.tier, spec.updates) section 11.2 (spec.agent) and section 12.18 (spec.backup; spec.database for the shared PostgreSQL, DB-SHARED-1). Every object is closed: a new field is a contract change first. The value UNVERIFIED marks a fact the scaffolder could not confirm from a primary source; it caps the app's tier at community.

apiVersion.description: onemind.app/v1 is the frozen manifest (PLAN-E6, E1). onemind.app/v1alpha1 is still accepted; app-manifest convert rewrites it to v1 without changing any other field.

id.description: DNS-1123 label; equals the apps/<id>/ directory name. At most 59 characters so the install namespace app-<id> (contract section 3) stays within the 63-character label limit.

publisher.description: Declared publisher identity; signature/index verification is required separately.

version.description: Upstream app version, as a string (quote it in YAML).

age_rating.description: Proposed minimum age for using the app: 0, 7, 12, 16 or 18. The rubric is in apps/README.md; when unsure, the higher number. It is the default for family filtering; an owner's own classification overrides it.

age_reason.description: One short line saying why the app has that age_rating, based on what the app does.

icon.description: Icon file path relative to apps/<id>/ (no leading slash, no '..').

license.description: SPDX license identifier or SPDX expression (e.g. MIT, Apache-2.0, 'Apache-2.0 OR GPL-2.0').

licenceClass.description: Market licence class of the app: L1 permissive and L2 copyleft are the green classes the Market shows and installs by default; blocked (source-available, non-commercial, proprietary) and unknown (not confirmed from the upstream licence) need an explicit owner confirmation to install. validate-apps checks that an L1 or L2 claim equals the class computed from metadata.license.

links.description: Upstream links shown in the Market (contract 9.3, 11.4).

github.description: https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>, or UNVERIFIED when the upstream is not on GitHub.

support.description: Where users report problems, usually the issue tracker.

upstream.description: Upstream release facts read from the GitHub API (contract 9.2, 9.3).

release.description: Upstream release tag, exactly as published.

tier.description: Set by CI (sdk/tools/app-gate), not by hand: verified, community or blocked (contract 9.4).

build.description: Present only when OneMind built the image itself (sdk/tools/app-factory): who built it, from which upstream release and base image, and what was patched.

revision.description: OneMind rebuild number for this upstream release.

base.description: The upstream image the build started from, by digest.

image.description: The OneMind-built image the manifests run.

egress.description: Internet egress hostnames (P9); default deny when absent or empty. Wildcards only below a registrable domain; the Go validator checks the embedded Public Suffix List.

bridge.description: Brings outside data in through gateway intake (POST /v1/bridges/<id>/events), never straight onto the map or another app (sdk/contracts/connectors.md). The source token is always the app id, so emits stay inside the app's own source.

mode.description: poll: fetches on a schedule. push: holds a stream open. dataset: a versioned file. local: the owner's own receiver, no internet.

connector.description: An outside account the owner connects (sdk/contracts/connectors.md): the gateway holds the credential and runs it; the manifest names only the auth type.

videoSource.description: A camera or video feed for the video engine. Metadata travels on the bus, frames never do. record needs a provider whose terms allow full display and storage.

nats.description: The app's own NATS account (APP_<id>): exact subjects under its own prefix, imports of named core subjects the owner approves, and limits shown in the install plan. No wildcards, no audit, requests or another app's subjects.

archs.description: CPU architectures the pinned images support.

requires.description: What a machine must have to run the app (#724), in the same shape as recommends and supports ($defs/machineNeeds): arch, memoryMb, storageFreeGb, accelerator, devices, radios and models. The older keys (gpu, minMemoryMb, gpuCount, minVramMb, cpuLevel, accelerator.optional) stay valid and mean the same thing; core/onemind_core/machine_needs.py maps them onto the new keys, and a manifest may not say one fact in both spellings. Memory is always stated (memoryMb, or the older minMemoryMb).

gpu.description: Older spelling: true means a required accelerator (accelerator: {capability: gpu-compute}).

gpuCount.description: Older spelling of accelerator.count: how many graphics cards the app needs (default 1). Only meaningful with gpu: true. The Market places the app on a machine that reports at least this many.

minVramMb.description: Older spelling of accelerator.minMemoryMb: memory the smallest graphics card must have, in MB. Only meaningful with gpu: true. A machine that does not report its card memory is not used (unknown is refused, never assumed).

accelerator.description: The accelerator the app needs, in vendor-neutral terms (S-5): $defs/machineAccelerator plus the older optional flag. The box reports what it has and the gateway maps one to the other; the app never names a vendor or a driver. Without optional: true the app is refused on a box that has none (with the older gpu key, gpu must then be true). optional: true is the older spelling of recommends.accelerator: the app runs without it and only gains speed.

cpuLevel.description: Older spelling of an x86-64 level in arch: lowest CPU level the pinned images need, per architecture. Install and update are refused on a box below it (NMD-09, #134). x86-64 levels follow the x86-64 psABI (-march=x86-64-vN). Omit when the images run on any CPU of the architecture.

recommends.description: What makes the app run better on a machine that has it (#724): the app still runs without it. A Market verdict says yes but slow when a recommended fact is missing, and not checked when the machine did not report it.

supports.description: What the app can use when a machine has it (#724), such as a radio, a device class or model quantisations; nothing is needed.

web.description: Web UI port. A Service in the rendered manifests must expose it.

browser.description: #692: a browser shown in a desktop window, one profile per person. The app's Deployment that mounts profileVolume is a template only (no replica, its Service is never proxied); the gateway makes one claim, pod and ClusterIP Service per signed-in person and serves each person only their own on <app>--<key>. Needs spec.web.

profileVolume.description: Name of the pod volume (backed by a PersistentVolumeClaim in the template) that holds the browser profile.

manifests.description: Kustomization directory relative to apps/<id>/ (no leading slash, no '..').

updates.description: Update policy (contract 9.3, 10.2): security-channel updates install automatically within the owner's policy; automerge patch lets Renovate merge green patch and digest bumps of a verified app.

credentials.description: PD-07: the app has a login the gateway generates at first install and stores sealed. Shown only to the owner (GET /v1/apps/{id}/credentials); the executor puts it in Secret <id>-credentials (keys USERNAME, PASSWORD) in app-<id>. Kept when the app is removed, erased with its data.

password.description: Only generated passwords: a default password in a public catalog is not a secret.

showBeforeOpen.description: The dashboard shows the login before it opens the app the first time.

agent.description: Agent principal for the app (contract 11.2): the gateway creates agent:<id> and the Secret <secret> in app-<id> at install.

secret.description: Secret name (DNS-1123 subdomain) that receives ONEMIND_GATEWAY_URL and ONEMIND_AGENT_TOKEN (and ONEMIND_GATEWAY_CA, the box CA as PEM, when the gateway is served over HTTPS).

settings.description: Owner-editable settings (contract 12.22): one JSON Schema subset per field, delivered as ConfigMap onemind-settings (keys = env). Settings are not secret; names that look like credentials are refused.

dependencies.description: Apps this app needs (contract 12.22): satisfied when id or any alternative is installed.

port.description: The provider's Service port this app calls (contract 12.22, dependency network paths). Default: the provider's spec.web.port.

desktop.description: The app streams a desktop to a browser tab (issue #786). Every workload of the app is then held to the desktop rules: non-root, unprivileged, the one runtime named by apps/_bases/desktop/base.yaml, and its own login off only behind the gateway's policy (sdk/tools/factorylib/desktop.py). Required for any app whose image is built FROM ghcr.io/onemindos/bases/desktop (such images carry the label com.onemindos.base=desktop) or that runs a streaming runtime.

runtime.description: Must be the runtime of the desktop base; the validator refuses any other.

base.description: Set when the app's image is built FROM the OneMind desktop base.

system.description: Marks a built-in (system) app. Only honoured for an app that lives in apps/_system/<id>/ AND whose id is on the signed /usr/lib/onemind/system-apps.json in the OS image; anywhere else the manifest is rejected. A system app cannot be uninstalled; it can be switched off (app.disable) unless disable is never. Switching off scales the workload to zero and keeps volumes, secrets and settings.

class.description: container: a workload in its own namespace. native: part of the OS or dashboard.

update.description: os: updated with the OS image. own: updated through its own channel (spec.updates).

disable.description: allowed: the owner may switch it off. never: it stays on (Files, Approvals, Settings, Market).

keepDataOnDisable.description: Data is always kept when an app is switched off; only true is accepted.

hostPorts.description: Host ports the app needs (contract 12.22). Default none. Conflict-checked across the catalog and per node; the install sandbox still refuses hostPort/hostNetwork in the manifests (F-05, F-01).

streams.description: Event streams the app keeps on the hub's JetStream (default none). Bounded: every stream needs a byte and an age limit, subjects are relative to the app (the hub puts them under onemind.plugin.<id>., the plugin kind of sdk/schema/onemind.subjects.json), and the owner approves the exact limits in the install plan. Enforced in core/onemind_core/streams.py.

backup.description: How the app is backed up (contract 12.18; BACKUPS.md 2.2). Without it the app is copied hot and its badge says crash-consistent only.

units.description: Built-in apps only (needs spec.system, which only the signed system apps list allows): the gateway tables and folders the app owns. The same block a built-in descriptor (onemind.builtin.schema.json) carries.

none.description: Why a built-in with an empty units list has nothing to back up.

mode.description: cold stops the app while it is copied

content.description: Large content the app downloads again by itself (offline libraries, map archives, model files): left out of backups like exclude until the owner switches the content tier on for the app after seeing its size (BAK-03, REC-NOMAD-07). Relative patterns, read like a relative restic --exclude.

secrets.description: Secrets the app needs (contract 12.18; docs/leap/core/SECRETS.md). Never values: the owner enters owner keys in the install approval, the box generates keys with generate: true, and the gateway writes each as a Kubernetes Secret in app-<id>.

name.description: Secret name (DNS-1123 subdomain), unique in the app and not the spec.agent Secret.

key.description: Data key in the Secret (often the environment variable name).

kind.description: How the form shows and checks it; default password.

required.description: Owner-entered and needed: the install cannot be approved without it.

generate.description: The box creates a random value at install and can rotate it; never entered.

not.description: A generated key is always set, so it is never also required; a url is never generated.

database.description: A database on the hub's shared PostgreSQL (DB-SHARED-1): at install the gateway creates database and role app_<id> and writes Secret <secret> in app-<id> with PGHOST, PGPORT, PGDATABASE, PGUSER, PGPASSWORD and DATABASE_URL. Dumps are part of the app's backups.

runtime.description: How the app runs (#604). module: in-process gateway code, only for an app on the signed system apps list (needs spec.system; plugin validate refuses it). container: its own workload (spec.manifests). none: declarative, drawn by the host.

placement.description: Where it may run: the hub, an edge machine, or either.

data.description: Data classes the app owns and reads (the same block a built-in descriptor carries), and how long it keeps them.

services.description: Shared services the app uses; the install card lists them.

search.description: The app's search provider: the item types it adds to the one local index (same as the built-in descriptor).

share.description: Share types the app accepts and what it does with them (same as the built-in descriptor).

notifications.description: Notification topics (same as the built-in descriptor). An app's ceiling is warning; action buttons call one of its own tools, and the host alone draws Review and Deny, never an Approve button.

mapLayers.description: Declarative map layers the shell draws (namespaced plug:<app>:<id>; no app JavaScript). source is a public read operation (built-ins) or emits: the layer emits of this app's bridge, served by the gateway.

jobs.description: Background runs of one of the app's own tools, as the app principal, within a time quota. A job never calls a destructive tool, and a write it makes is still a request a person approves.

roles.description: Default-app roles the app can fill; the owner picks one app per role.

continue.description: Screens that can continue on another device: the deep link onemind://app/<id><route> and the view-state keys handed over (never content).

needs.description: internet: a feature that cannot work offline, so the UI says so.

terms.description: The terms record (map-intel rule 2): the code licence is metadata.license; this holds every data provider's terms. Mandatory for an app with a bridge, connector or videoSource. personData is always false: no app tracks private individuals.

machineNeeds.description: One strength of what an app (and later a model, engine, simulator or bridge manifest) needs from a machine (#724): spec.requires (must have), spec.recommends (runs better with) and spec.supports (can use). Vendor-neutral names only: never a vendor resource such as nvidia.com/gpu, never a host path. A fact the machine did not report is unknown, never yes or no.

memoryMb.description: Memory of the machine, in MB.

storageFreeGb.description: Free space on the machine's data disk, in GB.

machineArch.description: CPU architectures, each named once. x86-64-v1 to x86-64-v4 mean amd64 at that x86-64 psABI level or newer (the older requires.cpuLevel.amd64). In spec.requires the architectures must be the ones spec.archs names (the images' own list).

acceleratorCapability.description: What the accelerator does, in vendor-neutral words (S-5). The node's hardware profile reports the same words.

minMemoryMb.description: Memory of the accelerator itself, not of the machine.

overlay.description: A directory next to spec.manifests (a kustomize overlay on it) that is rendered instead of the plain manifests on a box with this accelerator.

machineDevices.description: Reserved for bridges (#724): device classes in vendor-neutral words (for example serial-port or camera). Nothing grants a device yet; a later owner-approved grant passes one device node into one pod. Never a vendor resource such as nvidia.com/gpu, never a host path such as /dev/ttyUSB0.

machineRadios.description: Radios on the machine, by protocol (#724).

machineModels.description: Model files the app can run, by quantisation in lowercase (for example q4_k_m, q8_0, fp16, int8).

backupUnit.description: One thing a built-in module backs up from the gateway itself (#603). table: a gateway database table. dir: the folder a gateway setting (ONEMIND_*) names.

execHook.description: An argv command run inside the app's own container through the Kubernetes API (contract 12.18); never a host shell.

call.description: One public API operation, METHOD and OpenAPI path template (the same as onemind.builtin.schema.json $defs/call).

token.description: One lowercase NATS subject token (the token placeholder of sdk/schema/onemind.subjects.json).

toolRef.description: The name of a tool declared in spec.extensions.tools.

hostname.description: A plain internet hostname: lowercase, no wildcard, no port, no IP literal (the last label starts with a letter). It must also be listed in spec.egress.

natsSubject.description: A subject relative to the app's own prefix onemind.plugin.<id>. (the plugin kind of sdk/schema/onemind.subjects.json). No wildcards: NATS permissions are exact.

provider.description: One data provider's terms, as read by a person on readOn (map-intel rule 2). Install is refused without it; the gateway stamps licence and attribution on every value from this provider.

readOn.description: The date a person read the terms (YYYY-MM-DD, quoted in YAML).

use.description: What the terms allow: commercial use, non-commercial use only, or personal use only.

keyNeeded.description: The provider needs a key the owner enters (a spec.secrets entry, never a value here).

minIntervalSeconds.description: The provider's own polling floor; every block that reads this provider polls no faster.

store.description: none: show only. cache: keep for at most maxCacheSeconds. keep: may keep history.

redistribute.description: Whether values may leave the box: over the mesh, to TAK, or in a public share.

display.description: full: may be shown and restreamed. embed-only: only the provider's own player. link-only: a link out.

personScoped.description: Data belongs to one person's own account (such as an activity tracker) and is never shared on.

credentialValue.description: Not applied by the schema: the value patterns the one validator (core/onemind_core/manifest_rules.py and internal/plugin/validate/blocks.go) refuses in every string of a manifest, so no field can hold a credential. Errors name the field, never the value.

credentialName.description: Not applied by the schema: a field with one of these names may not hold a string (except the word generated, spec.credentials.password), anywhere in a manifest.

allOf.$comment: #604: runtime module is in-process gateway code, only for apps on the signed system apps list.
#604: the terms record is mandatory for every block that brings outside data in.
#604: a bridge or a NATS account is code that runs as the app principal in its own workload.
